policy_title: Improve Support for Children with SEND and Address School Costs
stated: Labour will take a community-wide approach to Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), improving inclusivity and expertise in mainstream schools while ensuring special schools cater to complex needs. They will require all schools to cooperate with local authorities on admissions, SEND inclusion, and place planning. To ease the cost of living, Labour will fund free breakfast clubs in every primary school and limit the number of branded uniform and PE kit items schools can require.

source.quote: Too often our education and care systems do not meet the needs of all children, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). Labour will take a community-wide approach, improving inclusivity and expertise in mainstream schools, as well as ensuring special schools cater to those with the most complex needs. We will make sure admissions decisions account for the needs of communities and require all schools to co-operate with their local authority on school admissions, SEND inclusion, and place planning. Labour will fund free breakfast clubs in every primary school, accessible to all children. Our breakfast clubs will support parents through the cost-of-living crisis. We will also bring down the cost of school by limiting the number of branded items of uniform and PE kit that schools can require.

bearing_set.reason: The SEND community-wide approach directly affects school standards, attainment gap for pupils with disabilities, and access to appropriate education — core O7 indicators.

Free breakfast clubs in every primary school reduce daily food costs for families, and capping branded uniform/PE kit items cuts a known household expense — both directly affect disposable income for families with school-age children.

membership_note: Two fundamentals: the SEND and breakfast-club strands bear squarely on educational opportunity and attainment (O7), while the breakfast clubs and uniform-cost cap are concrete levers on household essential costs (O2). Fiscal effects are unspecified in the stated policy and cannot be routed to O12 without a sourced costing. No material effect on healthcare, personal liberty, inequality (beyond what is captured within O7's attainment-gap indicator and O2), or other fundamentals clears the non-negligible bar.
